title: 听力模拟测试
goal: 完成长对话、听力篇章和讲座的信息理解题。

points.label: 完成长对话的信息理解题
完成听力篇章的信息理解题
完成讲话报道讲座的信息理解题

sources.title: 大学英语六级（CET-6）：课表
sources.used: 模拟测试的材料与课程掌握标准

body.p: 听力包含长对话、听力篇章和讲话、报道、讲座。三类材料分别对应 8、7、10 题，听力时间共 30 分钟，录音播放 1 遍。
长对话每段 280—320 词，听力篇章每篇 240—260 词，讲话、报道、讲座共约 1200 词。

audio.intro: Listen to a conversation between Maya and Daniel.

lines.text: Daniel, have you had a chance to look at the plans for the community book exchange? The library has offered us a corner near the entrance, but we need to decide how the shelves should work.
I have. The entrance is convenient, although it gets crowded when the afternoon classes finish. I'd rather not put a table right beside the door. People need room to pass.
That's a good point. The wall opposite the noticeboard is free. A narrow shelf there would leave the main route clear, and visitors would still see it as they come in.
Could we use the taller shelf in storage? It holds more books, but some visitors might not be able to reach the top. A lower shelf would be more accessible.
I agree. We can start with the lower one and keep extra books in boxes behind the desk. Volunteers could replace books on the shelf when there is space.
What about keeping records? We originally proposed writing down every book that came in or went out. That might take more time than our volunteers have.
Instead, let's count the books on the shelf at the start and end of each week. That won't tell us every title exchanged, but it will show whether the shelf needs more frequent attention.
Fine. I'll ask the library whether we can use the lower shelf and the space opposite the noticeboard. Could you prepare a short sign explaining that visitors may take a book or leave one?

Yes. I'll also ask the volunteers which day they can check the shelf. Once we've heard from the library, we can agree on a starting date. We should give volunteers enough notice to fit the checks around their other commitments.

items.stem: What are Maya and Daniel mainly discussing?
options: How to organize a book exchange inside a library
How to reduce crowding at the library entrance
How to record every title in a library collection
How to train volunteers to run the library desk
items.why: 两人讨论书架位置、高度、记录和志愿者安排，均围绕 community book exchange，即第一项。

items.stem: Why does Daniel object to a table beside the door?
options: The noticeboard already occupies that space.
The area becomes crowded when classes finish.
Visitors would not see the books as they came in.
The storage boxes would be inaccessible behind it.
items.why: it gets crowded when the afternoon classes finish 是不在门边放桌子的原因，即第二项。

items.stem: Why do the speakers prefer the lower shelf?
options: It holds more books than the taller shelf.
It can be placed behind the library desk.
Visitors can reach its contents more easily.
Volunteers can store extra boxes of books on it.
items.why: some visitors might not be able to reach the top 和 lower shelf would be more accessible 对应第三项。

items.stem: What does Maya agree to do?
options: Ask permission to move the noticeboard
Record the title of every book exchanged
Ask the library about the lower shelf
Prepare a sign explaining the exchange
items.why: Maya 同意 prepare a short sign explaining that visitors may take a book or leave one，即第四项。

audio.intro: Listen to a conversation between Leo and Nina.

lines.text: Nina, I'm arranging the interviews for our report on the town's bicycle repair service. The manager can speak to us on Tuesday morning or Thursday afternoon. Which would suit you?
Thursday would be better. I have a class on Tuesday, and I don't want to miss the chance to ask about their training program. Have you decided where we'll meet?
The manager suggested the repair room. We could see the equipment there, but it's noisy when several repairs are underway. A nearby meeting room might be better for recording.
Let's ask whether we can start in the meeting room and visit the repair room afterward. That way the conversation should be clear, and we can still see how the work is organized.
Good idea. I was planning to focus on the number of bicycles repaired. But the manager's message also mentioned that some customers only need advice, so those visits wouldn't appear in that count.
Then we should ask how the service records both repairs and advice. We can also ask whether demand changes across the year. I don't think we should assume that a busy week represents every month.
Agreed. I'll send the manager our questions in advance and confirm the rooms. Would you be able to check the recording equipment before Thursday?
Yes. I'll test the microphone and bring spare batteries. After the interview, I can make notes from the recording while you review the service's published figures.

That division works. We'll compare the figures with the interview before drafting the report, and we'll make clear which information comes from each source. If the figures cover a different period from the manager's examples, we'll say so. The dates will help readers understand which comparisons are possible.

items.stem: Why does Nina prefer Thursday afternoon?
options: The manager is unavailable at the repair service on Thursday.
The repair room is quieter on Thursday afternoon.
She has a class during the alternative Tuesday appointment.
She plans to review the published figures on Thursday morning.
items.why: I have a class on Tuesday 说明 Nina 选择周四的原因，即第三项。

items.stem: Why do the speakers propose starting in a meeting room?
options: It has more repair equipment available to inspect.
Visitors can watch how the work is organized there.
The manager suggested holding the interview there.
The recording may be clearer away from repair noise.
items.why: repair room ... noisy 和 meeting room might be better for recording 表明录音环境更安静，即第四项。

items.stem: What does Nina suggest asking about the service's records?
options: How both repairs and advice visits are counted
How many bicycles the service repairs each year
How the service keeps records of its equipment
Why advice visits are kept out of the records
items.why: ask how the service records both repairs and advice 对应第一项。

items.stem: What will Leo do before the interview?
options: Prepare notes from the completed recording
Send questions and confirm the meeting rooms
Test the microphone and obtain spare batteries
Draft the report from the interview responses
items.why: I'll send the manager our questions in advance and confirm the rooms 对应第二项。

lines.text: A small town recently reopened a footpath beside its river. For several months the path had been closed while workers repaired a damaged section of its surface. The closure affected a route used by people walking between a residential area and a bus stop. During the work, signs directed walkers along a longer street route. The repair team replaced the damaged surface and improved drainage near the lowest part of the path. Water had collected there after heavy rain, making the surface difficult to use. The team also checked the barriers beside the river, but the barriers did not need to be replaced. When the path reopened, a local group organized a walk to help residents learn about the changes. The walk began at the bus stop and ended near the residential area. Volunteers pointed out the repaired section and explained why the drainage work had been included. Some participants asked whether the path would remain open during future maintenance. The town said that short closures might still be necessary when work was being carried out. It also said that notices would be placed at both ends of the path when a closure was planned. The project did not create a new route across the river. Its purpose was to restore an existing connection and address a recurring problem on one part of that route. Residents can report future problems to the town's maintenance office, which will use those reports alongside its regular inspections.

items.stem: Why was the footpath closed?
options: Barriers beside the river needed replacing.
Workers needed to repair part of its surface.
A new route across the river was being built.
A bus stop beside the path was being rebuilt.
items.why: closed while workers repaired a damaged section of its surface 对应第二项。

items.stem: What problem did the drainage work address?
options: Damage to the barriers along the side of the river
The extra distance of the longer street route
The damaged surface along the whole length of the path
Water collecting on a low section after heavy rain
items.why: Water had collected there after heavy rain 说明改善排水的原因，即第四项。

items.stem: What did volunteers do during the reopening walk?
options: Show the repaired area and explain the drainage work
Replace the barriers along the river during the walk
Direct residents to a newly built route across the river
Promise that the path would never close for maintenance
items.why: pointed out the repaired section and explained ... drainage work 对应第一项。

items.stem: What did the town say about future maintenance?
options: Resident reports would replace the town's regular inspections.
The path would close permanently after the next inspection.
Short closures could occur, with notices placed at both ends.
Only the bus stop end would display a closure notice.
items.why: short closures might still be necessary 和 notices ... at both ends 对应第三项。

lines.text: A local theater has begun lending costumes to community groups between its own productions. The idea arose when staff noticed that many costumes remained in storage for long periods. Several neighborhood organizations were interested in staging small performances but had limited budgets for clothing. The theater decided to test a lending arrangement for one season. Groups apply in advance and describe how they intend to use the costumes. Theater staff then check which items are available and whether the proposed dates conflict with a production. Before an item leaves, staff record its condition and explain the cleaning instructions. Borrowers agree to return it by a specified date. The theater does not charge for the costume itself, but borrowers are responsible for cleaning it as instructed. If an item needs a repair, the staff discuss the problem with the borrowing group when it is returned. The theater also keeps some especially delicate items out of the lending collection. During the first part of the season, staff found that clear return dates made it easier to prepare costumes for the theater's own productions. They also found that checking items together with borrowers reduced confusion about their condition. At the end of the trial, the theater plans to ask groups about their experience and calculate the staff time involved. These records will cover applications and returns. The decision to continue will depend on both the value to community groups and the work required to maintain the collection.

items.stem: Why did the theater consider lending costumes?
options: Every costume was already needed for a theater production.
Community groups had asked to buy the stored costumes.
Unused costumes could help groups with small budgets.
Staff wanted to reduce the work of cleaning costumes.
items.why: costumes remained in storage 和 groups ... limited budgets 说明试行借用的原因，即第三项。

items.stem: What must borrowers do?
options: Buy each costume before the theater can lend it
Clean the costume according to the instructions
Repair any damage before returning the costume
Return the costume only after the theater's next production
items.why: borrowers are responsible for cleaning it as instructed 对应第二项。

items.stem: What will inform the decision to continue lending?
options: Only the number of costumes in storage before the trial
Only the dates of performances held by the theater
Only the staff time spent on applications
Its value to groups and the upkeep work it needs
items.why: value to community groups 和 work required to maintain the collection 是决定依据，即第四项。

lines.text: Today we'll consider how an object's label can shape a visitor's understanding of a collection. A label does more than supply a name. It can connect an object to a use, a place, a date, or another object. The information selected depends on the question the display is intended to address. Imagine a collection of containers used to carry water. One arrangement might group them by material: a clay vessel beside another clay vessel, and metal containers on a separate shelf. A label in that display might explain how the material affects the container's weight or durability. Another arrangement might group the same objects by the people who used them. In that case, labels could describe different activities for which water was carried. Neither arrangement changes the objects. It changes the relationship that is easiest for visitors to notice. Labels also have limited space. Adding more detail can provide useful context, but it can make a label harder to read quickly. A display team may choose to put a short description beside the object and offer a longer account in a separate booklet. This division allows a visitor to identify the object without requiring every visitor to read the full account at once. The booklet still needs to make clear which object each description concerns. A number or a small image can provide that connection. Consider a fictional exhibition in which visitors often confused two similar containers. The staff added a drawing of each object's handle beside its name. After the change, more visitors correctly matched the two names to the objects in a short survey. That observation suggests that the drawing may have helped, although other features of the display could also have influenced visitors. The survey alone cannot establish exactly where visitors looked. It is also limited to that exhibition and the people who responded. A display team could collect further evidence by asking visitors what information they used. The team could also compare answers from visitors who had and had not consulted the booklet. That comparison would identify a difference in responses, although it would still need careful interpretation because visitors choose whether to read the booklet. The purpose of these examples is to distinguish an object's physical features from the information used to interpret it. The choice of grouping and label affects which connections are made visible. A useful label is therefore related to the display's purpose and to the conditions under which visitors encounter it.

items.stem: What is the lecture mainly about?
options: How grouping and labels shape what visitors notice
How the material of a container affects its weight
How a booklet can replace labels beside objects
Why visitors should read a complete booklet before entering
items.why: grouping and label affects which connections are made visible 概括讲座主题，即第一项。

items.stem: Why does the speaker compare two arrangements of containers?
options: To show which arrangement visitors prefer
To show the same objects can reveal different relationships
To argue that a label should describe only an object's material
To explain how containers were used to carry water
items.why: Neither arrangement changes the objects. It changes the relationship ... 对应第二项。

items.stem: What limits the conclusion about the drawings of handles?
options: The survey established exactly where every visitor looked.
The drawings were added after the survey was done.
The visitors were asked to compare objects from every exhibition.
Other display features might also have affected the result.
items.why: other features of the display could also have influenced visitors 限定解释，即第四项。

lines.text: A fictional research team has reported on a comparison of two ways to remind people about appointments at a community center. The team wanted to know whether the timing of a reminder was associated with attendance. It did not attempt to compare appointments with no reminder against appointments with a reminder. All participants received the same message. Participants had already booked appointments for a consultation at the center. The researchers assigned half to receive the message one week before the appointment. The other half received it one day before. Both messages included the appointment time and the center's address. The team recorded whether each person attended the booked appointment. In the imagined results, a larger proportion of the one-day group attended. The team also recorded cancellations, but it did not treat a cancellation as attendance. Some people who canceled arranged another time, and those later appointments were outside the comparison. The researchers suggested that a reminder closer to the appointment might be easier to remember. They did not test participants' memory directly, so that suggestion remains a possible explanation rather than a measured result. The two groups received identical wording, allowing the comparison to focus on timing. Nevertheless, the research took place at one center over a limited period. It does not establish that the same difference will occur for every service or every group of participants. Another limit concerns the outcome. Attendance was recorded, but the study did not ask whether the message helped participants find the building or prepare questions. Those outcomes would require additional measures. A follow-up project could compare different kinds of appointment or ask participants how they used the reminder. It could also examine whether a message sent one day before gives enough time to cancel if a conflict arises. The center might also examine the staff time needed to manage cancellations. That practical question is separate from whether the reminder helped people remember their appointment, and the present study did not measure it. The current report separates the question, the assigned conditions, the observed difference, and a suggested explanation. It illustrates why even a controlled comparison should be described with its actual sample and outcome. A finding about attendance under these conditions is useful for the center's planning, but it is not a complete account of how all reminders affect all appointments.

items.stem: What differed between the two participant groups?
options: The kind of appointment each person had booked
The appointment address in the message
The time at which the same reminder was sent
The decision to receive any reminder at all
items.why: one week before 与 one day before 是相同提醒的不同发送时间，即第三项。

items.stem: What did the fictional comparison find?
options: More people in the one-week group attended.
A larger share of the one-day group attended.
Every cancellation became an attended appointment.
Both groups received different appointment addresses.
items.why: a larger proportion of the one-day group attended 对应第二项。

items.stem: Why is easier recall treated as a possible explanation?
options: The team measured every participant's memory directly.
The researchers did not record appointment attendance.
Participants received the reminder at identical times.
The team did not test participants' memory directly.
items.why: They did not test participants' memory directly 说明解释未被直接测量，即第四项。

lines.text: I'd like to discuss how a small organization can assess a proposal to share equipment. Suppose several local groups each own a folding table. They use their tables on different days, and some tables remain unused for long periods. Sharing might reduce the need to buy additional tables, but it also creates tasks that individual ownership does not require. A shared system needs a way to reserve an item and identify who is responsible for it at a given time. One possible arrangement is a calendar showing when each table is available. A group would request a date, collect the table, and return it afterward. The calendar could prevent two groups from expecting the same table at the same time. It would also need to be updated when a reservation changes. A second consideration is transport. If a table must be carried between buildings, the time and effort involved are part of the cost of sharing. A table stored centrally might reduce travel for some groups while increasing it for others. The groups should compare those journeys before choosing a location. Maintenance is another shared responsibility. A damaged hinge may need repair even if no group knows when the damage occurred. The groups could agree in advance on a method for reporting damage and deciding how repairs will be funded. Such an agreement would not prevent every problem, but it could make the response clearer. There are potential benefits as well. A group that needs an extra table only occasionally may avoid buying one if a shared table is available when needed. The space that would have been used for storage might also be used for another purpose. These benefits depend on actual availability. A reservation system that is difficult to use, or a table that is often unavailable, may not provide the expected saving. The groups could test the arrangement with one table for a limited period. During that trial they could record reservations, transport time, maintenance needs, and occasions when a request could not be met. They should also ask users whether the calendar and collection process were understandable. A trial would provide information about the conditions in which sharing took place, rather than guarantee that a larger system would behave identically. The decision to expand would require comparing the avoided purchases and other benefits with the work of coordination, transport, and maintenance. The central point is that a shared resource can create value, but the arrangements that make it available are themselves part of the decision.

items.stem: What is the main purpose of the talk?
options: To show that all local groups need tables on the same day
To explain how to repair a damaged table hinge
To weigh the gains and duties of sharing equipment
To explain why every organization should own extra tables
items.why: 讲述比较 avoided purchases 与 coordination, transport, and maintenance，评价共享设备的收益与责任，即第三项。

items.stem: What problem could a reservation calendar address?
options: Two groups expecting the same table at once
Every hinge becoming damaged during transport
The need to carry a table between buildings
Reports of damage that no group can explain
items.why: prevent two groups from expecting the same table at the same time 对应第一项。

items.stem: Why should transport be considered when choosing storage?
options: A central site guarantees the same journey for every group.
The time and effort of moving tables are costs of sharing.
Transport removes the need to maintain a reservation calendar.
All groups use their own tables in the same building.
items.why: the time and effort involved are part of the cost of sharing 对应第二项。

items.stem: What does the speaker suggest recording during a trial?
options: Only the purchase price of every table in the town
Only the names of the groups that already own tables
The exact results a larger sharing system would produce
Reservations, transport, repairs, and unmet requests
items.why: record reservations, transport time, maintenance needs, and occasions when a request could not be met 对应第四项。
